action: Organisations that send email through Cuenote FC: ask Ymir Link which of your lists were taken, assess whether you must notify recipients, and warn them about fake emails. Recipients: be cautious of unexpected messages from brands you subscribe to.
exec: A breach at an email-sending supplier exposed its customers' mailing lists at large scale, which may create notification duties for them.
plain: Japanese email-delivery company Ymir Link says a total of about 47.86 million mailing records leaked from 49 systems of its Cuenote FC service. No payment card data is confirmed leaked.
summary: In its third report, dated 11 November, Ymir Link says program vulnerabilities were exploited and information leaked from 49 Cuenote FC systems: a total of 47,864,147 records (about 47.86 million). It revised down an earlier estimate of 51,628,280 after removing double-counted records. Email addresses are in all 47,864,147; the report says no payment card data is confirmed leaked.
title: Ymir Link: a total of 47,864,147 records leaked from 49 Cuenote FC systems, company says

validation.note: Company's own third report (primary) and Socket's summary of it. Company says a final report follows the external forensic report.

review.note: Title, 47.9M records, 49 systems, Oct 19 first disclosure and Nov 11 update against Socket; single_source and aggregator tier are honest
